campaign: Snapshot-addressed code manifest and deterministic verification planning
doctrine: The code manifest is a generated structural authority, not a hand-maintained description. It must reuse the source snapshot, build selection, function profiling, reference census, and automation ownership already present in the repository. Generated facts and reviewed exceptions remain separate. Every manifest is canonical and bound to exact source bytes, analyzer version, build contexts, generated and non-Go inputs, and explicit uncertainty. Gate exclusion requires affirmative structural proof; missing analysis, reflection, cgo, unresolved interfaces, excluded build variants, generated inputs, or producer failure may broaden verification but may never silently narrow it. The manifest planner runs before selectable verification, emits an immutable plan for unchanged candidate bytes, and records why every check ran or was excluded. No duplicate parser, package inventory, call graph, ownership table, arbitrary fallback, or checked-in bulk manifest is introduced.

items.title: Bind execution and commit admission to the exact planned candidate

steps.title: Bind every gate result to the candidate snapshot, manifest, impact closure, gate plan, check definition, and relevant input identities
steps.rationale: A valid plan cannot authorize different bytes or changed check definitions after analysis.

steps.title: Require a successful unchanged-candidate plan before commit admission and preserve skipped, reused, failed, and inapplicable outcomes distinctly
steps.rationale: The preflight plan becomes authoritative only when commit admission verifies its identity and complete terminal evidence.

items.title: Persist manifests and reuse analysis without weakening identity

steps.title: Publish canonical manifest, delta, impact, plan, and selection evidence to the durable artifact store and provide bounded inspection summaries
steps.rationale: Bulk generated state belongs in content-addressed storage; commits reference identities instead of duplicating large JSON documents.

steps.title: Reuse package and manifest results by exact snapshot, analyzer, build-context, generator, and external-input identities with owned bounded eviction
steps.rationale: Incremental analysis must reduce gate latency without accepting stale structural facts or creating an unbounded cache.

items.title: Make the manifest selector falsifiable and adopt it across the repository

steps.title: Run fixed bootstrap checks for analyzer changes and fall back to the complete gate set whenever manifest planning cannot establish authority
steps.rationale: Manifest-selected checks cannot be the only protection for the analyzer that selects them.

steps.title: Add fixed change-to-required-check cases for interfaces, reflection, cgo, generated files, build tags, device code, schemas, fixtures, and non-Go authority
steps.rationale: The selector must be tested primarily against silent under-selection; safe over-selection remains measurable rather than forbidden.

steps.title: Migrate path-based selectors, publish exclusion, uncertainty, cache, latency, duration, and full-plan parity metrics, and require an uncached audit for releases
steps.rationale: Efficiency and conservatism must remain observable during rollout and release verification.

steps.title: Expose affected symbols, risk boundaries, ownership, required checks, exclusions, and prior evidence to agent change planning without allowing agents to self-declare safety
steps.rationale: Agent decisions and commit admission should consume the same measured structural authority.
